question: is the C->D move a change of coordinate on one trace?
answer: No. C is the full Hecke (Ocneanu/Wenzl) trace; D is the Temperley-Lieb/SU(2) QUOTIENT with y_(1^3) = 0. z is not a free coordinate but the rank label of z_N = q^N/[N]_q (D = N=2), and b^2 = [3]_q/[2]_q^2 makes the #6889 'degeneracy' exactly the non-semisimple locus of H_3(q).
corrects: the FRAMING of my #6915 and #6921 (measurements stand), and the INTERPRETATION of my merged #6889 (arithmetic stands, exclusion withdrawn)
scope: (b) for the identities and registry facts. Adjudicates neither ruling; proposes no replacement derivation.

assertions.name: D_annihilates_the_sign_block_C_does_not
assertions.detail: registry: D is named 'SU(2)/Temperley-Lieb (Jones) decomposition' with y_(1^3) = '0'; C is 'full-Hecke Ocneanu / Wenzl z-trace' with y_(1^3) = 0.0227449425... Both normalise (D: sum y_l d_l = 1; C: 1). TL_n = H_n/<antisymmetriser> kills every partition with >2 rows, which at n=3 is exactly (1^3). So D is a QUOTIENT of C — the two conventions differ in which blocks EXIST, not in how one object is coordinatised.

assertions.name: the_zD_equals_q2_zC_of_q2_relation_is_a_value_coincidence
assertions.detail: z_D(q) = q^2 z_C(q^2) holds exactly — which is what made the 'same form, different variable' reading tempting. It relates parameter VALUES only. Given assertion 1 it cannot be an isomorphism of traces: no substitution carries a 3-block trace to a 2-block one. This is why #6915's rescaling route was malformed rather than merely unsuccessful.

assertions.name: z_is_indexed_by_RANK_and_D_is_the_SU2_member
assertions.detail: z_N = q^N/[N]_q satisfies the full-bar condition bar(z) = z - h for every N = 1..6 (residual {'0'}), with twist N=1: q**(-2), N=2: q**(-4), N=3: q**(-6). z_2 = q**3/(q**2 + 1) = z_D, so D is the SU(2) member. z_C = 1/[2]_sqrt(q) has NO q^N numerator, is bar-even (twist 1) and is in the family for no N. The q^N numerator IS the bar twist — so rescaling z_D to bar-evenness strips the rank label.

assertions.name: b_squared_is_three_over_two_squared_so_its_vanishing_is_NONSEMISIMPLICITY
assertions.detail: b^2 = [3]_q/[2]_q^2 exactly (the variant q^2[3]/[2]^2 is NOT equal — my first attempt carried that spurious q^2 and sympy caught it, recorded because the wrong form is easy to reach). H_n(q) is semisimple iff [k]_q != 0 for all k <= n, so b^2 = 0 <=> [3]_q = 0 <=> H_3(q) is NOT semisimple. The pi/3 and 5pi/3 phases that #6889 called 'degenerate' — and used to declare the root-of-unity sublocus EMPTY — are exactly where the Wedderburn decomposition tr = sum_l y_l chi^l ceases to exist. #6889's arithmetic stands; its exclusion is WITHDRAWN as an interpretation.

assertions.name: TL_is_a_two_row_truncation_of_the_tower
assertions.detail: the 2026-09-03 owner ruling asks derivations to use the FULL TOWER (all n of H_n(q), all orders in q); the 2026-08-15 ruling makes D canonical. D = SU(2)/TL keeps only <=2-row partitions, so at n = 3A it discards the overwhelming majority of the tower. The two rulings pull opposite ways for this channel. MEASURED here, NOT adjudicated — which governs Q_beta is an owner decision.
